exposure: BMI category (based on US and Chinese guidelines)
GWG category (based on US and Chinese guidelines)
cohort: 2,271 pregnant women receiving perinatal care at Fooyin University Hospital in Taiwan from 2016 to 2021
finding: Increasing BMI and GWG are associated with higher risks of gestational diabetes, gestational hypertension or preeclampsia, Cesarean section, and Large for Gestational Age, while underweight women with excessive GWG had lower preterm birth risk, with notable differences in gestational hypertension or preeclampsia risk when comparing US and Chinese guidelines.
mod_finding: The study found no significant difference in Cesarean section rates based on BMI and GWG when using either US or Chinese guidelines.
